practica: Cosecha comunitaria de castaña por ribereños no indígenas en Roraima
periodo: Práctica documentada en Caroebe, Roraima, en 2023; transmitida desde la infancia

fuente.label: Souza, Oliveira et al. (2023) — Harvesting Bertholletia excelsa in a western Amazon rural community: local ecological knowledge and meaning to nut-crackers, Journal of Ethnobiology and Ethnomedicine 19: 61

verificacion: Most of the interviewees began collecting in childhood to help their families, and the activity was seen as important for family sustenance.

practica: Cosecha y replante deliberado de castaña por el pueblo Kayapó
periodo: Documentado mediante entrevistas en aldeas Kayapó del sureste amazónico en 2009-2011; publicado en 2014

fuente.label: Ribeiro, Jerozolimski et al. (2014) — Anthropogenic Landscape in Southeastern Amazonia: Contemporary Impacts of Low-Intensity Harvesting and Dispersal of Brazil Nuts by the Kayapó, PLoS ONE 9(7): e104271

verificacion: The Kayapó intentionally plant Brazil nut seedlings and seeds; this dispersal-harvesting combined strategy does not reduce the density of mature trees.

practica: Policultura agroforestal con fuego de baja intensidad en la cuenca del Tapajós
periodo: Documentada arqueobotánicamente en los últimos 4500 años en el sitio Serra do Maguari-1, Belterra (Pará)

fuente.label: Maezumi, Alves, Robinson et al. (2018) — The legacy of 4,500 years of polyculture agroforestry in the eastern Amazon, Nature Plants 4(8): 540-547

verificacion: Our data indicate that increases in canopy trees, palms and crop plants, combined with decreases in herbaceous plants, suggest a trajectory of short-cycle cultivation-fallowing with low-intensity burning over 4,500 years.

practica: Agricultura ribeirinha adaptativa ante inundaciones en la várzea del Solimões
periodo: Documentada en las reservas de Mamirauá y Amanã (Amazonas) en 2021

fuente.label: Ávila, Clement, Junqueira, Ticktin y Steward (2021) — Adaptive management strategies of local communities in two Amazonian floodplain ecosystems in the face of extreme climate events, Journal of Ethnobiology 41(3): 409-426

verificacion: Floodplain farmers managed diverse crop assemblages distributed across small upland plots, family gardens, communal areas, and secondary forests, adjusting production according to the hydrological phase.

practica: Ingeniería hidráulica xinguano: trasmallos, lagunas y corrales de tortugas
periodo: Complejo documentado arqueológica y etnográficamente entre los Kuikuro del alto Xingu; publicado en 2007

fuente.label: Heckenberger, Russell, Toney y Schmidt (2007) — The legacy of cultural landscapes in the Brazilian Amazon: implications for biodiversity, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 362: 197-208

verificacion: Weir fishing was still practiced at the time of study; artificial ponds and turtle corrals were largely abandoned during the twentieth century. These hydraulic features formed part of a broader cultural landscape from 800–1500 CE that integrated agriculture, aquaculture, and fishing.

practica: Cultivo temprano de manioc y zapallo con formación de tierra negra antrópica en el alto Madeira
periodo: Evidencia arqueobotánica del Holoceno temprano y medio (~9000-3000 AP) en Teotônio, Rondônia

fuente.label: Watling, Shock, Mongeló, Almeida, Kater, De Oliveira y Neves (2018) — Direct archaeological evidence for Southwestern Amazonia as an early plant domestication and food production centre, PLoS ONE 13(7): e0199868

verificacion: The macrobotanical remains from Teotônio include Manihot esculenta (manioc), Cucurbita sp. (squash), and Caryocar sp. (pequiá), along with one of the oldest Amazonian dark earth sequences yet documented.

practica: Manejo de plantas alimenticias por los Huni Kuĩ (Kaxinawá) en el bajo río Jordão, Acre
periodo: Documentado en tres comunidades de la TI Kaxinawá do Baixo Rio Jordão; publicado en 2023

fuente.label: Pilnik, Argentim, Kinupp, Haverroth y Ming (2023) — Traditional botanical knowledge: food plants from the Huni Kuĩ indigenous people, Acre, western Brazilian Amazon, Rodriguésia 74: e00482021

verificacion: A total of 89 native food plant species were recorded, with 60% used within active production systems. The most frequent category was semi-wild plants: species that germinate spontaneously near paths or disturbed areas and are then cared for or transplanted.

practica: Jardines criollos multiestratos con café en Haití
periodo: Sistema documentado en 28 fincas de los departamentos Nord y Grande-Anse de Haití; publicado en 2024

fuente.label: Millet, Allinne, Vi, Marraccini et al. (2024) — Haitian coffee agroforestry systems harbor complex arabica variety mixtures and under-recognized genetic diversity, PLoS ONE 19(4): e0299493

verificacion: The Jardin Créole system combines fruit and timber trees in the upper stratum with cacao, banana, and plantain in intermediate levels, and yam and taro below. The system dominates Haitian coffee production with minimal inputs and preserves greater arabica genetic diversity than many intensified farms.
